name: MonarchProvenance
title: Provenance
summary: Where a value came from and how fresh it is, such as "Registry · 2 hours ago".
whenToUse: Next to any value the product did not get from the user: data from a registry, an import or a calculation, so people can judge how far to trust it.
whenNotToUse: For the freshness of a whole data set with a refresh button, use MonarchFreshnessIndicator. For an AI-generated value, use MonarchAiGeneratedBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchProvenance(source: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchProvenanceVariant = MonarchProvenanceVariant.Chip, checkedAt: Long? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchProvenanceLabels = MonarchProvenanceLabels())
class MonarchProvenanceLabels(source: ((source: String) -> String)? = null, checked: ((time: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: source
options.description: Where the value came from, already localised. Nothing is drawn when it is empty.

options.name: variant
options.description: Chip is a small bordered tag; Inline is plain muted text.

options.name: checkedAt
options.description: When the value was fetched, checked or computed, in epoch milliseconds (UTC); shown as relative time and redrawn every minute.

options.name: icon
options.description: A decorative icon before the text. Hidden from TalkBack.

options.name: onClick
options.description: Makes the note a button that opens the source record. The app navigates.

states.name: with time
states.description: The source, a middle dot and the relative time.

states.name: opens the source
states.description: The source in the link color and underlined; the note is a button with a 48dp touch target.

appearance: Caption text in the muted text color. The chip adds the subtle background and the subtle border with small rounded corners; the inline form has neither. When it opens the source, the source takes the link color and an underline. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows the absolute time in a tooltip on hover and focus; touch has no hover, so TalkBack reads the relative time that is shown, as on iOS. The web source can be any content; here it is text. The web href turns the source into a link; components do not navigate on Android, so onClick makes the whole note a button and the app opens the record. Dates are epoch milliseconds, formatted with DateUtils because java.time needs API 26. iOS shares the name and the variants.
accessibility: The note is one TalkBack element read as "Source: Registry, checked 2 hours ago"; the icon and the middle dot are hidden.
With onClick the note has the button role and a touch target of at least 48dp, reserved in the layout.
The link state is shown by an underline as well as the color.
The text wraps at the largest font size instead of being cut off.
edgeCases: A time in the future reads as "in 5 minutes".
The relative time is redrawn once a minute while the note is on screen.

examples.title: Next to values
Inline, opening the source record
examples.code:
MonarchProvenance(
    source = "Imported file",
    variant = MonarchProvenanceVariant.Inline,
    onClick = { /* open the import */ },
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web underlines the age ("2 hours ago") with a dotted line because hovering it shows the absolute time in a tooltip. Touch has no hover, so the dotted line would suggest a tap target that does not exist.
parityExceptions.convention: Material guidance: no hover tooltips on touch; do not mark non-interactive text as interactive
